rounds.q: What year was the first email sent between two computers?
rounds.why: Its inventor also picked the @ sign to split a person's name from their computer's.
rounds.src: Internet Hall of Fame, Official Biography: Raymond Tomlinson (1971)
rounds.fun: Email dates all the way back to 1971. That is one old inbox!

rounds.q: What year was the first computer mouse built?
rounds.why: It was a wooden box that rolled on wheels, not a ball.
rounds.fun: The very first mouse was made of wood. Squeak squeak, click!

rounds.q: What year did a car first go faster than 60 mph?
rounds.why: It was an electric car, going 68 mph. By 1900, a third of all vehicles were electric.
rounds.src: IEEE history wiki; US Dept. of Energy (1899 and 1900)
rounds.fun: Zoom! An electric car hit 68 mph way back in 1899.

rounds.q: What year did the world's first traffic light go up?
rounds.why: It ran on gas lamps in London. The first electric one came in 1914, in Cleveland.
rounds.fun: London had a traffic light 46 years before Cleveland got an electric one!

rounds.q: What year was the fax machine first patented?
rounds.why: The telephone wasn't patented until 1876, a full 33 years later.
rounds.src: IEEE/ETHW, Fax Machines; Library of Congress, Bell Papers timeline (1843/1876)
rounds.fun: Faxes beat phones by 33 years. Beep boop, paper incoming!
